standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphism in a precategory
standard_prerequisites.statement: An isomorphism from a to b is a quadruple (f, g, eta, epsilon) with eta : 1_a = g o f and epsilon : f o g = 1_b.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose propositionality is asserted, and the two witnesses compared in the proof are such quadruples.

standard_prerequisites.name: Hom-sets are sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: In a precategory the types hom_A(a,b) are sets.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the identity types of hom-sets mere propositions, so that only the first components need comparing at source line 102.

standard_prerequisites.name: Precategory axioms
standard_prerequisites.use: The displayed chain at source line 104 uses the unit and associativity laws to identify g with g'.

core_obligations: Take two isomorphisms (g, eta, epsilon) and (g', eta', epsilon') from a to b and reduce the goal to the equality of the underlying morphisms (source lines 100-102).
Justify that reduction: since hom-sets are sets, their identity types are mere propositions, so the coherence data need not be compared (source line 102).
Show g = g' by the displayed chain g' = 1_a o g' = (g o f) o g' = g o (f o g') = g o 1_b = g, in which eta and epsilon' are the two identities consumed (source lines 103-105).
Conclude that the type of isomorphisms is a mere proposition, hence that a ~ b is a set (source lines 96-97).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to comparing the underlying morphisms.
Identify the two morphisms by the unit and associativity laws.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.1.3 at source lines 95-98: for any morphism f the type of proofs that f is an isomorphism is a mere proposition, hence the isomorphism type a ~ b is a set. The author's proof (source lines 99-106) is short but it contains a real reduction: two candidate isomorphisms carry four components each, and the proof discards the coherence data by observing that the identity types of hom-sets are mere propositions (line 102) before identifying the underlying morphisms through a five-term chain that consumes exactly two of those components, namely eta and epsilon' (lines 103-105). The statement is a propositionality claim and records neither the reduction nor which witnesses are used.
